This protocol was frozen as version 1.0 after verification of source-file structure, variable coding, geographical compatibility and age-group mapping, and before examination of substantive utilisation results.

# Background and rationale

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have become an increasingly important therapeutic class in diabetes and weight management. Their uptake has changed rapidly following the introduction of newer active substances, particularly semaglutide.

French individual-level studies using the Système national des données de santé (SNDS) have previously characterised initiation, indications and potential misuse of GLP-1 RAs. However, access to individual-level SNDS data is restricted.

Open Medic provides annual, aggregated and openly accessible data derived from the SNDS. These data permit transparent and reproducible analyses of reimbursed medicines dispensed in community pharmacies, including beneficiary counts, reimbursed boxes and expenditure measures.

This study is intended as an open and reproducible drug-utilisation analysis. It will extend existing French evidence through 2025 and examine national, demographic and regional patterns while documenting the analytical capabilities and limitations of aggregated reimbursement data.

# Research question

How did reimbursed community use of GLP-1 receptor agonists evolve in France from 2019 through 2025, nationally and according to age, sex and region of residence?

# Objectives

## Primary objective

To describe annual numbers and population rates of beneficiaries with at least one reimbursed community dispensing of a GLP-1 RA in France between 2019 and 2025.

## Secondary objectives

1. Describe annual reimbursed box counts, reimbursement base and reimbursed expenditure.
2. Characterise class-level utilisation according to age and sex.
3. Characterise crude and age-sex-standardised regional utilisation rates.
4. Describe changes in utilisation by active substance.
5. Quantify regional variation and its evolution over time.
6. Compare aggregate trends with previously published French studies using individual-level SNDS data.
7. Document the strengths and limitations of Open Medic for pharmacoepidemiological research.

# Study design

This will be a repeated annual cross-sectional drug-utilisation study using aggregated administrative reimbursement data.

Each calendar year will constitute a separate cross-sectional observation period. Individuals cannot be linked between years, between active substances or between geographical units.

The study is descriptive and population-level. It will not estimate causal effects or comparative effectiveness and will not evaluate safety, treatment adherence or persistence.

# Study setting and period

The primary study period will be 1 January 2019 through 31 December 2025.

The primary geographical scope will be France entière, including metropolitan and overseas regions where Open Medic categories can be matched reliably to INSEE denominators.

A sensitivity analysis restricted to metropolitan France will be conducted if overseas data present material denominator, coding or comparability limitations.

Open Medic records are dated according to reimbursement date rather than prescription or dispensing date.

# Data sources

## Open Medic complementary databases

The primary source will be the annual Open Medic complementary databases enriched with beneficiary counts, produced by the Caisse nationale de l’Assurance Maladie.

These databases contain aggregated information on medicines dispensed in community pharmacies and reimbursed by French mandatory health-insurance schemes. They cover the general scheme, the agricultural scheme and special schemes.

The following annual archives will be used for 2019–2025:

* Open Medic ATC4 complementary archives;
* Open Medic ATC5 complementary archives.

The anticipated analytical files are:

* `NB_YYYY_ATC4`;
* `NB_YYYY_ATC4_AGE_SEXE`;
* `NB_YYYY_ATC4_REG`;
* `NB_YYYY_ATC4_AGE_SEXE_REG`;
* `NB_YYYY_ATC5`.

ATC5 demographic or regional files will only be incorporated if explicitly added to the statistical analysis plan before substantive results are examined.

Open Medic reports:

* beneficiary counts;
* reimbursed box counts;
* reimbursement base;
* reimbursed expenditure.

The source archives and extracted files will be preserved as immutable raw data. Download dates, release dates, URLs, file sizes and SHA-256 checksums will be recorded in a machine-readable manifest.

The corrected version of the 2025 regional data released after 10 July 2026 will be used. Corrected ATC4 files for 2023 and 2024 will also be verified through recorded checksums and download dates.

Official source: [Assurance Maladie — Open Medic complementary databases, 2014–2025](https://www.assurance-maladie.ameli.fr/etudes-et-donnees/open-medic-depenses-beneficiaires-medicaments).

## INSEE population estimates

Population denominators will be obtained from INSEE regional population estimates by sex and five-year age group.

For calendar year $y$, the preferred denominator will be the estimated average population:

$$
N_y =
\frac{
  N_{\text{1 January } y}
  +
  N_{\text{1 January } (y+1)}
}{2}
$$

This calculation will be performed within each compatible region, age and sex stratum. It approximates the population exposed during the calendar year more closely than a single beginning-of-year estimate.

The January 2026 INSEE release provides the required regional series through 1 January 2026, allowing calculation of the average 2025 population.

INSEE estimates identified as provisional will remain eligible but will be labelled accordingly. The downloaded workbook, source URL, file size and SHA-256 checksum are recorded in `data/metadata/reference_manifest.csv`.

Official source: [INSEE — Population estimates by region, sex and age, 1975–2026](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/8721456).

# Study population

The numerator population will consist of beneficiaries represented in Open Medic with at least one reimbursed community dispensing during the relevant calendar year and aggregation level.

The denominator population will consist of residents represented in the corresponding INSEE population estimate.

The resulting measures will be interpreted as population-based rates of reimbursed dispensing beneficiaries. They will not be described as disease prevalence or treatment prevalence without qualification.

Potential differences between the health-insurance beneficiary population and the resident population will be acknowledged as a numerator–denominator limitation.

# Pharmacological definition

## Primary definition

The primary GLP-1 RA definition will be the ATC4 class:

* `A10BJ`: glucagon-like peptide-1 analogues.

Class-level beneficiary counts will be obtained directly from ATC4 files.

Beneficiary counts from individual ATC5 substances will never be summed to estimate unique GLP-1 RA users because one beneficiary may receive more than one active substance during the same year.

## Included active substances

The ATC5 substances within `A10BJ` are:

* `A10BJ01`: exenatide;
* `A10BJ02`: liraglutide;
* `A10BJ03`: lixisenatide;
* `A10BJ04`: albiglutide;
* `A10BJ05`: dulaglutide;
* `A10BJ06`: semaglutide;
* `A10BJ07`: beinaglutide.

All codes belonging to `A10BJ` will remain in the prespecified code list, regardless of whether they are observed in French reimbursement data during the study period. Absence from Open Medic will be reported as not observed rather than treated as a retrospective exclusion.

## Excluded treatments

The following will not be included in the primary definition:

* `A10BX16`: tirzepatide;
* `A10AE54`: insulin glargine and lixisenatide;
* `A10AE56`: insulin degludec and liraglutide.

Tirzepatide is a dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist classified outside `A10BJ`. Fixed combinations of insulin and a GLP-1 RA are also classified outside `A10BJ`.

Any broader analysis of incretin-based therapies will be prespecified, analysed and reported separately. It will not replace or be merged with the primary `A10BJ` analysis.

The authoritative machine-readable definition is maintained in:

```text
data/metadata/atc_codes.csv
```

# Measures

## Primary measure

The primary measure will be the annual class-level beneficiary rate per 100,000 residents:

$$
R_y =
\frac{U_y}{N_y}
\times 100{,}000
$$

where:

* $U_y$ is the ATC4 beneficiary count for calendar year $y$;
* $N_y$ is the estimated average resident population for year $y$.

The corresponding annual beneficiary count will also be reported.

## Secondary measures

Secondary measures will include:

* annual number of reimbursed boxes;
* reimbursed boxes per 100,000 residents;
* reimbursed boxes per beneficiary;
* reimbursement base in nominal euros;
* reimbursed expenditure in nominal euros;
* reimbursed expenditure per beneficiary;
* percentage change from the previous year;
* cumulative percentage change between 2019 and 2025;
* compound annual growth rate over 2019–2025;
* active-substance-specific beneficiary counts;
* active-substance shares of boxes and expenditure.

Active-substance beneficiary counts will be presented independently. They will not be expressed as mutually exclusive shares expected to sum to 100%.

Box counts will not be interpreted as equivalent treatment quantities because package sizes, doses and dosing schedules can differ between products and over time.

Expenditure will initially be reported in nominal euros. Any inflation-adjusted analysis will require a prespecified price index and will be labelled as a secondary analysis.

# Demographic analyses

Class-level utilisation will be described using the official Open Medic age and sex categories.

The age categories are:

* `0`: 0–19 years;
* `20`: 20–59 years;
* `60`: 60 years or older;
* `99`: age unknown.

INSEE five-year age groups will be aggregated as follows:

* 0–19 years: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14 and 15–19 years;
* 20–59 years: 20–24 through 55–59 years;
* 60 years or older: 60–64 years through 95 years or older.

The Open Medic sex categories are:

* `1`: male;
* `2`: female;
* `9`: sex unknown.

Age-specific rates will use the corresponding aggregated INSEE age denominators. Sex-specific rates will use the corresponding sex-specific denominators.

The primary age-sex analyses will use the six combinations of the three known age groups and two known sex categories.

Unknown age (`99`) and unknown sex (`9`) categories will be retained in raw and harmonised data and quantified for quality-control purposes. They will be excluded from analyses requiring a population denominator and will not be redistributed or imputed.

# Regional analyses

Regional analyses will use the beneficiary region of residence recorded in `BEN_REG`.

The known Open Medic regional codes will be interpreted as follows:

* `5`: overseas regions and departments combined;
* `11`: Île-de-France;
* `24`: Centre-Val de Loire;
* `27`: Bourgogne-Franche-Comté;
* `28`: Normandie;
* `32`: Hauts-de-France;
* `44`: Grand Est;
* `52`: Pays de la Loire;
* `53`: Bretagne;
* `75`: Nouvelle-Aquitaine;
* `76`: Occitanie;
* `84`: Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes;
* `93`: Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur and Corse combined.

Codes `0` and `99` represent an unknown or unspecified beneficiary region. They will be retained for quality control but excluded from region-specific rates and maps.

The primary regional analysis will therefore comprise 13 geographical units: 12 metropolitan groupings and one combined overseas grouping.

Regional population denominators will be constructed from the corresponding INSEE regions. In particular:

* the denominator for code `93` will be the sum of Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur and Corse;
* the denominator for code `5` will be the INSEE `DOM` aggregate;
* the national denominator will be the INSEE `France métropolitaine et DOM` aggregate.

For each regional unit and year, the following will be reported:

* beneficiary count;
* crude beneficiary rate per 100,000 residents;
* age-sex-standardised beneficiary rate per 100,000 residents;
* absolute and relative change over time;
* rank based on the standardised rate;
* absolute and relative deviation from the national standardised rate.

Regional heterogeneity will be summarised using:

* minimum and maximum;
* median and interquartile range;
* maximum-to-minimum ratio;
* coefficient of variation.

Metrics that are unstable because of very small or disclosure-controlled values will not be reported without an explicit sensitivity analysis.

The primary cartographic outputs will show:

1. the crude regional beneficiary rate in 2025;
2. the age-sex-standardised regional beneficiary rate in 2025;
3. the percentage change in the crude regional beneficiary rate between 2019 and 2025.

Official administrative geometries will be used. Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur and Corse will receive the same value corresponding to Open Medic code `93`. The overseas regions included in code `5` will likewise receive the same combined value and will be clearly identified as an aggregated Open Medic unit. Unknown regional categories will not be mapped.

Maps will display descriptive regional variation and will not be treated as evidence of spatial dependence. No spatial autocorrelation or spatial regression model is prespecified in the primary analysis.

# Direct standardisation

Regional beneficiary rates will be standardised directly using six common age-sex strata defined by the three Open Medic age groups and two known sex categories.

The standard population will be the estimated average population of France entière in 2025, calculated as the mean of the INSEE populations at 1 January 2025 and 1 January 2026. The six standard-population weights will sum to one.

For region $r$, year $y$, and age-sex stratum $s$:

$$
R^{\mathrm{std}}_{ry}
=
\sum_s
w_s
\left(
\frac{U_{rys}}{N_{rys}}
\right)
\times 100{,}000
$$

where:

* $U_{rys}$ is the regional beneficiary count;
* $N_{rys}$ is the corresponding estimated average regional population;
* $w_s$ is the proportion of the 2025 standard population in stratum $s$.

Records with unknown age or sex will not contribute to stratum-specific rates. The proportion excluded for this reason will be reported for each region and year whenever it can be calculated validly.

Crude and age-sex-standardised rates will be reported together. Standardised rates will be interpreted as comparative summary measures and not as observed population rates.

# Active-substance analysis

ATC5 files will be used to describe substance-specific utilisation.

For each substance and year, the study will report, where available:

* beneficiary count;
* reimbursed boxes;
* reimbursement base;
* reimbursed expenditure;
* boxes per beneficiary;
* expenditure per beneficiary.

The sum of substance-level beneficiary counts will not be compared with the ATC4 beneficiary count as if the two estimands were equivalent.

For additive measures such as boxes and expenditure, the sum across included ATC5 codes will be compared with the corresponding ATC4 total as a quality-control check.

Differences will be investigated in relation to coding, unknown categories, file corrections or classification changes.

# Statistical analysis

The primary analysis will be descriptive.

Annual national and regional estimates will be presented using tables and figures. Because Open Medic represents aggregated administrative counts rather than a probability sample, conventional sampling-based confidence intervals will not be used as the primary expression of uncertainty.

Trend summaries will include absolute change, percentage change and compound annual growth rate.

No causal effect, treatment effect or individual-level association will be estimated.

No null-hypothesis significance testing is planned for the primary analysis.

Any regression model added for descriptive trend summarisation must be specified in the statistical analysis plan before it is fitted.

# Disclosure control and unknown categories

Open Medic applies disclosure control when the critical threshold of ten beneficiaries is not met. Certain affected dimensions may be represented using unknown codes such as `9`, `99` or `999`.

These categories will:

* be identified using official documentation;
* never be interpreted as ordinary substantive categories;
* be retained in raw and harmonised data;
* be quantified in quality-control reports;
* not be redistributed or imputed in the primary analysis.

National totals will be obtained from the appropriate national aggregation file rather than reconstructed by summing lower-level files.

Regional and demographic analyses will disclose the proportion of beneficiaries assigned to unknown categories whenever it can be calculated validly.

# Quality-control procedures

Quality control will include:

1. Verification of archive integrity and SHA-256 checksums.
2. Verification of expected filenames and archive contents.
3. Comparison of schemas across years.
4. Verification of column types and coding systems.
5. Verification of the sign, range and numerical type of beneficiary, box and expenditure measures.
6. Verification of uniqueness for expected aggregation keys.
7. Detection of duplicated rows.
8. Verification of study years and ATC codes.
9. Identification of unknown and disclosure-controlled categories.
10. Comparison of national totals across compatible aggregation files.
11. Comparison of additive ATC5 measures with corresponding ATC4 totals.
12. Independent reproduction of selected totals in Python and R.
13. Confirmation that corrected 2023–2025 source files are used where applicable.

Negative beneficiary counts (`nbc`) are not expected and will be classified as a critical quality-control failure.

Negative values in reimbursed boxes (`BOITES`), reimbursement base (`BSE`) or reimbursed expenditure (`REM`) may reflect reversals, corrections or other accounting adjustments in the source data. They will therefore be retained unchanged and classified as quality-control warnings rather than automatically treated as errors.

Negative values will not be converted to absolute values, truncated to zero or imputed. Their frequency and magnitude will be documented by year, file and measure. Their presence in records contributing to the study population will be assessed, and a sensitivity analysis excluding affected records will be conducted if their influence on a reported estimate is material.

Critical quality-control failures will stop the analytical pipeline. Documented warnings, including permissible negative accounting measures, will not stop the pipeline unless they materially compromise a planned analysis.


# Sensitivity analyses

Planned sensitivity analyses include:

1. Using the population at 1 January of each study year instead of the average annual population.
2. Restricting geographical analyses to metropolitan France.
3. Comparing crude and age-sex-standardised regional rates.
4. Excluding unknown demographic or geographical categories from stratified analyses while retaining national direct totals.
5. Reporting tirzepatide separately as an expanded incretin analysis if observable and relevant.
6. Assessing the impact of provisional INSEE population estimates.
7. Comparing estimates reconstructed from stratified files with directly reported national estimates.

Sensitivity analyses will not be used to redefine the primary estimand retrospectively.

# External comparison

Aggregate trends will be compared descriptively with previously published French studies based on individual-level SNDS data.

This comparison will be described as external triangulation or reproducibility assessment, not validation.

Differences in estimands will be made explicit. In particular, individual-level studies may identify incident users, treatment indications, switching or clinical characteristics, whereas Open Medic provides annual aggregated beneficiary and dispensing measures.

# Interpretation boundaries

Open Medic does not directly measure:

* prescriptions written;
* medicines actually taken;
* clinical indication;
* treatment initiation;
* switching;
* persistence;
* adherence;
* clinical effectiveness;
* safety outcomes;
* non-reimbursed use.

Regional and demographic findings will be interpreted as aggregate descriptive variation. They will not be interpreted as individual-level effects or causal relationships.

The study will avoid ecological inference from regional characteristics to individual beneficiaries.

# Data governance and ethics

Only open, aggregated and disclosure-controlled data will be used.

No individual-level records, personal identifiers or personal health data will be accessed or processed.

The study is not intended to make decisions concerning individual patients.

Applicable source licences and attribution requirements will be documented. Third-party data will not be relicensed by the project.

# Reproducibility

The project will use:

* Git for version control;
* Python for acquisition, extraction, harmonisation and initial quality control;
* Parquet for shared analysis-ready datasets;
* R for epidemiological analysis, standardisation and visualisation;
* Quarto for protocol, white paper and portfolio publication;
* `pip-tools` for Python dependency locking;
* `renv` for R dependency locking.

Raw source data will not be committed to Git. Their provenance and reconstruction procedures will be documented through manifests, checksums and executable code.

# Protocol amendments

Changes made before version 1.0 is frozen will be incorporated into the protocol and version history.

After version 1.0 is frozen, any change affecting:

* the research question;
* primary pharmacological definition;
* study period;
* primary measure;
* denominator;
* standard population;
* inclusion or exclusion rules;
* principal statistical analysis;

will require a dated protocol amendment containing:

1. the original specification;
2. the revised specification;
3. the reason for the change;
4. whether results had been examined;
5. the expected analytical impact.

# Pre-analysis decisions resolved

The following pre-analysis decisions were resolved using official source documentation and structural inspection conducted before examination of substantive utilisation results:

* Open Medic source column names, canonical column names and inferred data types are documented in the annual column inventories.
* Historical differences in column-name capitalisation are harmonised without modifying the source files.
* Official age, sex and unknown-category definitions are specified in this protocol.
* The mapping between Open Medic age categories and INSEE five-year age groups is specified.
* The `BEN_REG` regional mapping, included territories and required INSEE aggregations are specified.
* Annual Open Medic archive names, source URLs, download dates, file sizes and SHA-256 checksums are recorded in machine-readable manifests.
* Compatibility of the 2019–2025 schemas has been verified after canonicalisation.
* The primary direct-standardisation procedure uses six age-sex strata and the estimated average population of France entière in 2025 as the standard population.
* The selected INSEE workbook and annual worksheets for 2019–2026 are recorded in the reference-data manifest.
* ATC4 data provide the primary class-level beneficiary estimates. ATC5 data provide substance-specific estimates and will not be summed to estimate unique class beneficiaries.
* Additive ATC5 measures, including boxes and expenditure, will be compared with corresponding ATC4 totals as quality-control checks.
* Negative beneficiary counts are classified as critical failures. Negative box or monetary measures are retained unchanged and treated as documented accounting warnings unless they materially compromise an analysis.
* The principal national, demographic, regional, active-substance and cartographic outputs are prespecified in this protocol. Detailed presentation layouts may be refined in the statistical analysis plan without changing the estimands or analytical methods.

No substantive GLP-1 RA utilisation results were examined while resolving these decisions.

Implementation metadata, including downloaded geometry versions, checksums, software versions and presentation formatting, may be recorded or updated without a protocol amendment provided that the study population, estimands, definitions and analytical methods remain unchanged.


# Planned outputs

The study will produce:

* frozen protocol version 1.0;
* statistical analysis plan;
* ATC code list;
* source-data manifest;
* data dictionary;
* reproducible Python and R code;
* quality-control report;
* scientific white paper in English;
* executive summary in French;
* public portfolio page.
